title: An asymptotically solvable model of many-body critical phases: mobility edges, scars, and inverted scars
authors: Yi-Ting Tu, Zi-Jian Li, Sankar Das Sarma
abstract: While the prethermal regime of random many-body localized (MBL) systems is dominated by accidental many-body resonances, another class of resonances, originating from the underlying potential structure, is expected in large-size deterministic systems. It is known that this class of resonances can lead to single-particle critical phases that are neither localized nor extended, but the consequences in interacting systems remain unclear. In this work, we construct an asymptotically solvable model of a one-dimensional nearest-neighbor interacting spin chain, whose spatial structure induces a hierarchy of mirror-like many-body resonances. We derive two phases in the thermodynamic limit, characterized by the satisfaction and violation of a version of the weak eigenstate thermalization hypothesis (ETH). While these two phases are similar to the usual MBL and ETH phases, there exist rare eigenstates that behave like the opposite phase, interpreted as many-body scars and inverted scars. Surprisingly, the two phases can be separated by a finite-temperature phase transition, corresponding to a thermodynamic many-body mobility edge, which was often believed to be impossible. Our results also suggest the existence of delocalized rare regions in an otherwise-localized interacting Aubry-André model, even if there are no low-disorder regions like those in random systems. This challenges the common belief that there is no avalanche instability in quasiperiodic MBL.
summary: This work constructs an exactly solvable model of an interacting spin chain exhibiting a hierarchical mirror structure. It identifies two distinct many-body phases separated by a finite-temperature transition, suggesting a thermodynamic mobility edge in short-range systems. The findings challenge existing beliefs about localization and rare regions in quasiperiodic quantum matter.
main_problem: Investigating many-body critical phases beyond standard Many-Body Localization (MBL) by studying resonances arising from the underlying potential structure in deterministic, quasiperiodic systems.
main_result: The authors derive two distinct thermodynamic phases separated by a finite-temperature phase transition corresponding to a mobility edge, and suggest delocalized rare regions can exist even without low-disorder impurities.
method: Construction of an asymptotically solvable model for a 1D interacting spin chain using the concept of Hierarchical Mirror Structure (HMS) and analyzing ETH satisfaction/violation in the thermodynamic limit.
model_or_system: A one-dimensional nearest-neighbor interacting spin chain with a spatial structure inducing a hierarchy of mirror-like many-body resonances. The analysis also relates to the Aubry-André model.
key_observables: Weak Eigenstate Thermalization Hypothesis (ETH) satisfaction/violation; existence and nature of rare eigenstates (many-body scars and inverted scars); thermodynamic mobility edge.
important_parameters: Temperature, system size (thermodynamic limit), structural parameters defining the HMS hierarchy ($\Delta\phi_n$).
main_assumptions: The model is constructed to be asymptotically solvable; analysis relies on separating transport timescales across different levels of the resonance hierarchy.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates how interactions affect an HMS system, showing hierarchical oscillations, resonance at low levels, and protection mechanisms that can lead to freezing or delocalization.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the structural basis using the HMS concept derived from single-particle spectral analysis ($\mu_{sc}$), then constructs the asymptotically solvable interacting model, analyzes the resulting two phases (MBC-E/MBC-L) and their separation by a mobility edge, and finally discusses implications for quasiperiodic models.
why_interesting: It directly addresses critical phenomena in interacting quantum systems, extending concepts from MBL theory to deterministic structures and proposing novel phase transitions like the thermodynamic mobility edge.

(b) For the lowest level of the hierarchy, if a particle is near the mirror center, it is resonant between two mirrored sites (a and b). (c) Further away from the mirror center, the particle becomes non-resonant due to a small asymmetry between sites a′ and b′ (red dashed line). FIG. 3: Recursive construction of the solvable models, which works for both single-particle and many-body versions. At each step, Hres n+1 is formed by making a mirrored copy of Hres n (the resonant region), adding a pair of new segments Hnr n , g Hnr n with small symmetry-breaking terms Hβ n (the non-resonant region), and finally coupling the four segments by bonds Hγ n, Hαγ n , f Hγ n which are weaker and weaker as n →∞.

FIG. 4: Visualization of the eigenstates and their labeling of Hres n with Lres 1 = 1, Lnr n = n. The (i, j) entry of the matrix is ⟨j|ψi⟩n, assuming all error bounds are negligible. The figure is for illustrative purposes and not plotted from numerical data. The hierarchical structure is indicated at the bottom of the matrix, with magenta (gray) being (non-) resonance regions.

FIG. 5: Progressive approximations of the solvable model on an infinite lattice, which works for both single-particle and many- body versions. The Hamiltonian H∞ n at each step is a sum of decoupled segments. In the limit of n →∞, H∞ n converges to the final model H∞(in the sense of operator norm in the single-particle case, and term-wise in the many-body case).
